title: California maximum tenant screening fee (2026)
requirement: A landlord may charge a prospective tenant no more than the annual maximum screening fee ($68.96 for 2026) and must give the applicant a copy of any consumer credit report obtained, a receipt, an itemized expense list, and a refund of any unused portion.
coverage_conditions: All landlords charging tenant screening fees to prospective tenants in California.

applicability.per_tenancy: Applies when a landlord charges a screening fee to a prospective tenant.

quoted_span:
The maximum tenant screening fee for 2026 is
$68.96

title: California reusable tenant screening report requirement
requirement: If a prospective tenant provides a reusable screening report, the landlord must use it.
coverage_conditions: All landlords screening prospective tenants in California.

applicability.per_tenancy: Applies when a prospective tenant provides a reusable screening report.

quoted_span: If the tenant provides a reusable screening report, the landlord must use it.

title: Berkeley tenant screening fee disclosure and non-refundable application fee ban
requirement: An owner or agent who charges an applicant a screening fee must first give a tenant screening fee rights statement and the state maximum fee cap, and may not charge an existing tenant a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy or to add or replace a roommate.
coverage_conditions: All residential rental agreements in Berkeley, regardless of any contrary lease language.

applicability.per_tenancy: Applies to owners or agents charging applicants a screening fee, and to fees charged to existing tenants for renewals or roommate changes.

quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.
